failures.title: Jaguar AJD-V6 2.7 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Oil Pump Housing Failure - the defining failure
items.whatHappens: The oil pump housing is a critical weak point, particularly at the tensioner mount. When it cracks or fails, oil pressure drops rapidly, leading to immediate oil starvation and catastrophic engine damage. A sudden drop in oil pressure warning or metallic knocking from the bottom end is the primary early warning sign.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught extremely early, oil pump housing replacement is theoretically possible, but in practice most failures write off the engine due to rapid bearing and crankshaft damage. A full reconditioned or rebuilt unit is almost always required. Read our full oil pump failure guide .

items.title: Crankshaft Bearing Failure
items.whatHappens: Crankshaft bearing failure is typically a secondary consequence of oil pump housing failure or oil starvation. Symptoms include deep knocking from the bottom end, low oil pressure, and eventually engine seizure.
items.repairVsReplace: Bottom-end rebuild is possible but labour-intensive and expensive (£5,500-£7,000). Most specialists recommend a full reconditioned unit instead, as the root cause (oil pump housing design) remains unaddressed in a partial repair.

items.title: Turbocharger Failure
items.whatHappens: The twin-turbo setup is subject to wear at higher mileage, particularly if oil quality has been neglected. Symptoms include excessive smoke, loss of power, and whining noises from the turbo housings.
items.repairVsReplace: Turbo replacement is a standard repair (£1,200-£2,500 per turbo) and does not typically require a full engine replacement unless turbo debris has entered the oil system and caused bearing damage.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2007 AJD-V6 2.7 units received revised oil pump housing designs, but the fundamental design weakness remains - the failure is so intrinsic to the architecture that even revised units carry elevated risk compared to later Jaguar diesels .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the AJD-V6 2.7
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ The AJD-V6 2.7 is Jaguar's designation for the PSA/Ford-developed 2.7L "Lion" V6 diesel. While it shares its core architecture with the later 3.0L variant and the Land Rover 276DT, confirming your exact code is critical because internal components and engine management are not interchangeable. WHERE TO FIND THE CODE: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, usually visible near the bellhousing or on the cylinder head cover. It will also be explicitly listed on your V5C registration document under "Engine Code" or "Engine Capacity", and can be decoded directly from your 17-character VIN. COMMONLY CONFUSED CODES: - AJD-V6 3.0: The 3.0L successor introduced in 2009. While it shares the same basic V6 architecture, the 3.0L has different bore dimensions, revised internals, and updated engine management, making it a non-straight swap. - 276DT: Land Rover's designation for the exact same 2.7L engine. While mechanically identical, the engine loom, ECU, and mounting points may differ between Jaguar and Land Rover applications - confirm fitment before purchasing a Land Rover-sourced unit. Why fitting the wrong revision matters: Attempting to swap a 3.0L long block into a 2.7L chassis without updating the ECU, loom, and fuel system will result in persistent fault codes and poor drivability. Similarly, a Land Rover-sourced 276DT may require Jaguar-specific ECU mapping and loom adapters. CLOSING LINE: Not 100% sure? Enter your registration above - we'll confirm your exact AJD-V6 2.7 fitment before any quotes are sent.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement AJD-V6 2.7 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Jaguar AJD-V6 2.7 engine is only advisable if it comes with comprehensive, documented proof that the oil pump housing has already been replaced with a revised design. Without this specific history, the risk of inheriting the same catastrophic oil pump failure is unacceptably high. This option is generally reserved for higher-value host vehicles (e.g., a low-mileage XJ X350) where the budget is tight. Explore our vetted used Jaguar AJD-V6 2.7 engine network.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned Jaguar AJD-V6 2.7 engine is the most balanced and recommended choice for the majority of owners. A quality, specialist-led rebuild will systematically address the known weak points: upgraded oil pump housing design, new turbochargers, revised timing chain set, and all critical gaskets and seals. This effectively resets the engine's reliability clock and is the most cost-effective way to secure long-term peace of mind. Compare reconditioned Jaguar AJD-V6 2.7 engine options.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples, vehicles that have suffered from oil starvation, or if the crankshaft shows measurable damage. An upgraded rebuild should include a revised oil pump housing design, new crankshaft bearings, reground crankshaft, and new turbochargers, ensuring the engine can reliably handle another 100,000+ miles. View rebuilt Jaguar AJD-V6 2.7 engine specifications.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Buying through the EnginesMarket network means you can opt for a full supply and fit service, with the replacement engine installed by a Jaguar specialist and backed by a nationwide warranty. Learn more about supply and fit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The Jaguar AJD-V6 2.7 is typically found in host vehicles (like the S-Type X200 or XJ X350/X358) valued between £4,000 and £14,000 depending on condition and mileage. If your vehicle is at the lower end of this spectrum (e.g., an early S-Type valued under £6,000), a £5,000+ reconditioned Jaguar AJD-V6 2.7 engine replacement may approach or exceed 60% of the car's total current market value.
